 JUDGMENT
Initially this claim petition was filed seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
Unfortunately, during the pendency of the petition i.e., on 07.04.2022 the petitioner expired.
Thereafter his legal representatives got impleaded themselves in the petition .

Brief case of the petitioner in the nutshell:
2. The facts leading to the filing of the instant petition are that on 29.08.2021 at about 12.30 p.m, when he was riding the Honda Activa scooter bearing No.KA-03-KE-5190 on outer ring road, near Karthiknagar, by observing all the traffic rules at that time the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-NK-1436 came from hind side in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger the human life and dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle.
As a result of impact, petitioner sustained injuries all over the body.
It is further submitted that, after the accident he was shifted to V.Care Mediscon Hospital wherein he was treated as inpatient and during his treatment he undergone surgery.
It is stoutly pleaded that, petitioner has spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.

It is further submitted that, the petitioner was hale and healthy and working as Mechanic and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month and contributing his entire income to the family and the petitioner is the sole bread winner to his family.

It is further urged by the wife of the petitioner that after accident the petitioner was unable to walk, speak, squat and unable to do any work and was suffering from head ache and giddiness and memory problem.
It is specifically contended that the accident happened because of the shear negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-NK-1436.
It is further urged that, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner under all heads including the general damages.
Hence prayed to allow the petition.

sentences.text: 14. Repelling to the contentions urged by the petitioner, the respondent No.1 had attacked the case of the petitioner on various prisms known to fact and law.

The first limb of contention urged by the respondent is the petitioner himself is negligent and the next plank of contention urged is that, there is absolutely no nexus to the injuries sustained by the petitioner to his death.
Further denied all the allegations made in the petition.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.
In order to substantiate the above said factum the respondent No.1 did not choose to lead any evidence.
15. This issue revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the alleged rash and negligence on the part of the driver of car.

On marshaling of factual matrix, on dissection of evidence placed on record and after hearing on erudite counsel appearing for petitioner and respondent, this Tribunal opines that this issue is pregmented with inner issues such as :
1) Involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
2) Alleged rash and negligent act.

3) The authenticity of IMV report,
16.
Now let me unfurl each of the contentions urged by the combating parties with respect to the alleged negligence.
The rival parties are at logger heads with respect to the factum of negligence.
That is to say petitioner imputes rashness and negligence on the driver of offending car.
Whereas the insurance company contended that, petitioner sustained injuries due to the sole negligence and due to self fall from the motorcycle and he was the main architect to the accident.
17. Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.

These elements are as follows:
Duty:
For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.

At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.

In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.
18. Now let me test the factual matrix in the light of settled principle of law.
From the evidence placed on record it is crystal clear that, there is no qualm with the fact that, petitioner was a rider of the two wheeler.
The only dispute in controversy is as to the alleged rash and negligent act of the offending vehicle.
Now let me test the factual matrix in the light of settled principle of law.
The chargesheet was filed against the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-NK-1436 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 338 of IPC and 134(B), 187 of IMV Act.
19. Further the spot panchanama is marked as Ex.P.4.
On conspectus scrutiny of Ex.P.4 spot mahazar indicates that the accident in question was occurred in the manner of alleged by the petitioner.

Though it was strenuously urged by the respondent counsel with regard to alleged contributory negligence but despite incisive cross-examination, the insurance company could not elicit anything from the mouth of PW.1 to show that deceased was also responsible for the accident.

20. Added more there was nothing on record placed by the respondent No.1 to believe that, Ex.P.7 chargesheet filed by the police for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 338 of IPC in crime No.39/2021 of Airport Traffic Police is defective or collusive.
The whole anchorage of the defence of the respondent No.1 is on the bedrock of the contributory negligence on the part of petitioner himself.
But when this court gave its anxious consideration with astuteness to Ex.P.4 spot mahazar and Ex.P.5 spot sketch it could gather that the said accident had taken place in a straight road.
There is no curves what so ever in the said road.
If the driver of vehicle was moving on a normal speed then he could have certainly avoided the accident.
Further the respondent No.1 has denied the cause of the accident, but it has not lead any cogent evidence to prove its defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioner.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Mere self- serving rather self-proclaimed statement of the respondent cannot be trusted as a gospel truth.

21. Further the respondent No.1 did not make any attempt to examine the driver of offending car,
who is the best witness to depose about the cause of accident.
There is no explanation to that effect.
Non-examination of driver of the insured vehicle is fatal to the defence of the insurance company.
22. Further Ex.P.6 IMV Report goes to show that at the time of inspection both vehicles involved in the accident and sustained damages as detailed out in the said report.
Be that as it may, the IMV inspector has mentioned that he tested both the vehicles on road and found that their brake systems were intact.

Thereby he opined that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the said Mohammed Khaleel vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110393202/

23. ISSUE NO.2 :
During pendency of the petition, the petitioner cum injured - Sri. Mohammed Khaleel died and his legal representatives was brought on record.
Admittedly in the background of factual circumstances of the petition on hand, mere proof of actionable negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle is not sufficient.
In addition to that the claimant is required to establish that, there is nexus between the death of Sri. Mohammed Khaleel and the accidental injures suffered by him.
24. The main lis between the parties is with regard to the cause for death of the petitioner.
It is specifically contended by the LRs of the petitioner that, the petitioner has breathed his last because of injuries sustained in the RTA.
On the other hand the said contention is stoutly denied by the respondent No.1 and contended that, there is absolutely no nexus with the injuries sustained by the petitioner to his death.
When combating parties urged these contentions it is the burden bestowed heavily on the LR's of the petitioner to show the nexus of injury to the death.
On perusal of the petition averments it is clearly forthcoming that, the petitioner has met with an accident on 29.08.2021.
Furthermore order sheet dated 13.09.2022 reveals that the petitioner has expired on 07.04.2022.
It is pertinent to note that the LR of the deceased petitioners have produced Ex.P.13 being the death certificate of deceased petitioner.

On perusal of the same it clearly discloses that the petitioner was died on 07.04.2022 and further it discloses the place of death as No.159, 6 th Cross,
Inam Masjid Main road, Rshad Nagar, BBMP, Bengluru.
The moot question to be answered is with regard to the nexus of Injury and death.
25. In order to prove the nexus of death and injury there is absolutely no string of evidence produced by the petitioner No.1(a).

The petitioner No.1 has produced the wound certificate issued by Jeevika Hospital, Bengaluru which is marked as Ex.P.3 it discloses the injuries sustained by the petitioner are here under : Laceration over the scalp, occipital region, parietal region bleeding present.
At the same time it is relevant to note that as per Ex.P.14 the medical record of Jeevika Hospital it reflects that the patient was discharged as the patient was not willing to get admitted.
When this being the case, it can be presumed that he was stable at the time of discharge.
Apart from that there is no string of evidence produced before this court in order to show that he has taken treatment as inpatient.
26. Furthermore, another important aspect to be noted herein there is, no Postmortem was conducted after death of the petitioner.
Added more the LR's of petitioner after the death of petitioner has not given further complaint to the jurisdictional police by informing the death of the petitioner.
All these aspects adds to the fatality to the case of the petitioner.
The LR's of petitioner had averred in the affidavit that, petitioner had died because of injuries sustained in RTA.

27. Further more, when the PW.1 was subjected to litmus test of cross-examination wherein she categorically admitted as hereunder :

Further it could be ascertained from the documentary evidence after death, postmortem was not done and he has not filed any complaint with regard to the death of the deceased.

It is a ordinary prudent of a common prudent man that if a person at first sustained injury and then because of the injuries has breathed his last then same has will be intimated to the jurisdictional police and thereafter further complaint will be lodged.
In the instant case on hand the non action of LR's of petitioner itself vibrantly goes to show that, there is absolutely no nexus with the injuries with that of the death of the petitioner.

If the injured had sustained traumatic injuries then he might have not been in a position to give instructions to the counsel so as to file this petition.

no medical document spells about the fatal injuries sustained by the petitioner.

29. It is noteworthy to state that, the Postmortem examination of the deceased has not been conducted to find out the cause of his death.
Further the police have not filed Chargesheet against the driver of offending vehicle by invoking Section 304(A) of IPC.

30. In the absence of such proof, as per the ratio laid down in the decision reported in 2010 KAR MAC 557 between Somavva & others V/s Vijaya Kumar and others, the legal representatives of the deceased are entitled to claim only expenses spent towards the treatment of the deceased petitioner and the loss of income suffered by the deceased during laid-up/ treatment period.

sentences.text: 31. It is trite law that when the petitioner has failed to prove the income, the income of the petitioner has to be taken in to consideration as notional income.
The next moot question to be consideration is as to how the notional income has to be considered in the eye of law.

32. The learned counsel for the respondent argued vociferously by relying on the decisions of the Hon'ble High court of Division Bench in MFA No.7404/2014 dated 06.12.2022 in the case of Smt.
Mariyamma W/o. Hucchellappa & others V/s Suyambulingam.V & anr. In the above said decision it Mohammed Khaleel vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110393202/

By relying on this decision it is argued strenuously by the learned counsel for the respondent that, the notional income as fixed by Karnataka Legal Service Authority, cannot be taken into consideration and the court must dwell in to considering the notional income as prescribed under Minimum Wages Act.

33. Per Contra it is relevant to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV)
dated.05.07.2023.

sentences.text:
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
34.
It is pertinent to note that the Subordinate courts are governed under as per Article141 of Indian Constitution which deals with law of precedents.
The decision relied by the respondent counsel is rendered by the Division Bench of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the month of December- 2022.
The decision which is relied by the petitioner counsel is rendered by the Division Bench of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the month of July-2023.

As per the principles laid down by the plethora of decisions by Constitutional Courts it would be culled out in two decisions taking contradictary view by the Division Bench then recent one will prevail over the previous one.
When such is the case law rendered by the Division Bench of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) rendered in the month of July-2023 is binding on this tribunal.

As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority,
Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on 29.08.2021.
Therefore, Rs.15,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased petitioner.

35. As per the medical records the original petitioner has sustained the following injuries:
Laceration over the scalp, occipital region, parietal region bleeding present.
It is needless to say that the above injuries are mild, grievous in nature.
The petitioners have not produced the discharge summary.

But on perusal of records the discharge of V care is available and on perusal of the same it indicates that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital from 29.08.2021 to 04.09.2021 (7 days in total).

sentences.text: MEDICAL EXPENSES:
Medical bills which were produced by the petitioner are marked at Ex.P16.
As per that, the petitioner had spent Rs.47,692/- towards medical expenses.
All these bills have been meticulously examined and are found to be correct.
There is no contra evidence to disbelieve the bills.
Though respondent No.1 counsel had cross examined PW1 at length but nothing fatal has been elicited to distrust the version of PW1.
Hence an amount of Rs.47,692/- which is rounded off to Rs.47,700/- is awarded under this head.
37. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
The period of hospitalization of 7 days is proved.
Considering the nature of injuries and treatment given, it is quite natural that the deceased could not have carried out his avocation for atleast 2 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.30,000/- (15,000 X 2) under this head.
38.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
39. The petitioner being the Legal representative of the deceased (Sri. Mohammed Khaleel) is entitled for compensation of Rs.77,700/-.

The respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-NK-1436 are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the Legal Representative of the deceased petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the affirmative'.
40. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the findings given on issues No.1 & 2 and for the reasons discussed therein, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle's Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :

The Legal Representative of deceased petitioner is entitled to get compensation of Rs.77,700/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
After deposit, the entire compensation amount together with interest shall be released to the LR's No.1 of deceased petitioner through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor-in-office framed the following :
ISSUES 1. Whether the LR's of deceased petitioner proves that on 29.08.2021 at about 12.30 p.m while the petitioner was proceeding on his Honda Activa scooter bearing reg.No.KA-03-KE-5190 near Outer Ring Road, Karthiknagara, Bengaluru City, at that time, the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-NK- 1436 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle.
As a result, the petitioner fell down from the motorcycle and sustained grievous injury ?
2. Whether the LR's of deceased petitioner are entitled for compensation as prayed for ? If so, at what rate and from whom?
3. What order or award ?
9. This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1: The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to award a compensation of an amount to the tune of Rs.10,00,000/-.
The case of the petitioner lies an narrow compass as to claiming of compensation amount for injuries sustained by him in a Road Traffic Accident.
11. It is the case of petitioner that, on 29.08.2021 at about 12.30 p.m, when he was riding the Honda Activa scooter bearing No.KA-03-KE-5190 on outer ring road, near Karthiknagar, by observing all the traffic rules at that time the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-NK-1436 came from hind side in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger the human life and dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle.
15. This issue revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the alleged rash and negligence on the part of the driver of car.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Mohammed Khaleel vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110393202/
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
The chargesheet was filed against the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-NK-1436 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 338 of IPC and 134(B), 187 of IMV Act.
The whole anchorage of the defence of the respondent No.1 is on the bedrock of the contributory negligence on the part of petitioner himself.
There is no curves what so ever in the said road.
If the driver of vehicle was moving on a normal speed then he could have certainly avoided the accident.
Further the respondent No.1 has denied the cause of the accident, but it has not lead any cogent evidence to prove its defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioner.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Mere self- serving rather self-proclaimed statement of the respondent cannot be trusted as a gospel truth.
21. Further the respondent No.1 did not make any attempt to examine the driver of offending car,
who is the best witness to depose about the cause of accident.
There is no explanation to that effect.
Therefore the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-NK-1436 did not have sufficient cause to cause the accident.
25. In order to prove the nexus of death and injury there is absolutely no string of evidence produced by the petitioner No.1(a).
When this being the case, it can be presumed that he was stable at the time of discharge.
Apart from that there is no string of evidence produced before this court in order to show that he has taken treatment as inpatient.
In order Mohammed Khaleel vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110393202/
7 to substantiate above said factum there is absolutely no iota of documentary evidence is placed before the court.
Further it could be ascertained from the documentary evidence after death, postmortem was not done and he has not filed any complaint with regard to the death of the deceased.
It is a ordinary prudent of a common prudent man that if a person at first sustained injury and then because of the injuries has breathed his last then same has will be intimated to the jurisdictional police and thereafter further complaint will be lodged.
In the instant case on hand the non action of LR's of petitioner itself vibrantly goes to show that, there is absolutely no nexus with the injuries with that of the death of the petitioner.
This petition is filed on 23.12.2021 by the injured himself in his personal capacity.
If the injured had sustained traumatic injuries then he might have not been in a position to give instructions to the counsel so as to file this petition.
no medical document spells about the fatal injuries sustained by the petitioner.
When such being the case, there is absolutely no nexus with the injuries sustained and death of the petitioner.
Further the police have not filed Chargesheet against the driver of offending vehicle by invoking Section 304(A) of IPC.
Absolutely no iota of evidence is placed on record to prove that the deceased died on account of injuries sustained in the accident.
When such is the case law rendered by the Division Bench of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) rendered in the month of July-2023 is binding on this tribunal.
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.

opennyai_summary.decision:
The decision relied by the respondent counsel is rendered by the Division Bench of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the month of December- 2022.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.30,000/- (15,000 X 2) under this head.

39. The petitioner being the Legal representative of the deceased (Sri. Mohammed Khaleel) is entitled for compensation of Rs.77,700/-.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-NK-1436 are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the Legal Representative of the deceased petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the affirmative'.
40. ISSUE NO.3 :
In view of the findings given on issues No.1 & 2 and for the reasons discussed therein, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle's Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The Legal Representative of deceased petitioner is entitled to get compensation of Rs.77,700/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
After deposit, the entire compensation amount together with interest shall be released to the LR's No.1 of deceased petitioner through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
